title: Determination of Phosphorus: Ascorbic Acid Procedure
author: Unknown
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.ggcbtsw
materials: Niskin bottle
Nylon mesh filter (500 um)
Hot plate
Gloves
Scoop (0.4 g capacity)
125 mL Erlenmeyer flask
Acid washed glassware
Analytical balance
Spectrophotometer
Acid washed plastic bottle
0.7 um filter Acid Wash Procedure for Preparing Sampling Containers and equipment:
Wash each sample bottle or piece of glassware with a brush and phosphate-free detergent.
Rinse three times with the cold tap water.
Rinse with 10 percent hydrochloric acid.

Rinse three times with deionized water. For phosphorus analysis, sample water should be either grabbed or composite and, collected from the well-mixed areas of the water body so that they are representative of the total flow. Niskin bottles should be used to collect the sample water which will then filtered through a 300 um nylon filter and transferred to a 100 ml HDPE plastic bottle either made of high-density polyethylene or polypropylene (accepted by EPA). If the containers are to be reused, they must be washed repeatedly with HCl and, de-ionized water as the phosphorus molecule has the tendency to absorb (attach) to the inside surface of the container. The samples bottles will be then placed on a cooler having dry ice on it and transported immediately to the lab for further processing. Prior to final analysis or preservation, sample water should be filtered through a 0.7 um filter.
125 mL Erlenmeyer flasks (acid washed)
50 mL graduated cylinders (acid washed)
Phenolphthalein indicator
Sulfuric acid solution: 300 ml concentrated sulfuric acid and 1 L distilled water
Ammonium persulfate, crystal
Sodium hydroxide solution (1N): 40 g sodium hydroxide crystals and 1 L distilled water Procedure:
Sample water (50 ml) will be taken on an acid washed Erlenmeyer flask and diluted into 50 ml distilled water.

One drop of phenolphthalein indicator will be added and if a red color develops, then sulfuric acid solution (1 ml) will be added until color just disappears. If the color disappears, 0.4 g ammonium persulfate will be added.
The solution will then boil gently for 30 to 40 minutes or until the total volume is 10 mL.
Cool the solution and add 1 drop of phenolphthalein to neutralize to a faint pink color with 1 N sodium hydroxide.

Finally, the solution will be diluted with distilled water to make 50 mL solution and ready for total phosphate analysis. Preservation: If total Phosphorus is the only determination to be made, acidify the sample to less than pH 2 with sulfuric acid and cool to 4°C. Acidified and cooled samples may be held for up to 28 days.
Spectrophotometer with an infrared phototube for use at 885 nm with a light path of 10 cm
Ammonium molybdate solution: 15 g of reagent grade ammonium paramolybdate, (NH4)6Mo7O24 .4H2O and 500 ml of deionized water.
Ascorbic acid solution: 27 g of ascorbic acid and 500 ml of deionized water.
Sulfuric acid solution: 140 ml of concentrated sulfuric acid and 900 ml of deionized water.

steps.instruction: The phosphate concentration can be calculated by the following equation:Concentration of orthophosphate or total phosphate (umol l -1 ) = F * corrected absorbanceWhere:Corrected absorbance = sample absorbance - reagent blankF = standardization factorA standardization factor F can be calculated as:F = 3.0 umol/kg / (Es- Eb)Where:3.0 umol/kg = concentration of the standardEs = mean absorbance of the standardsEb = mean absorbance of the blanks References: Strickland, J.D.H., and Parsons, T.R. (1968). Determination of reactive phosphorus. In: A Practical Handbook of Seawater Analysis. Fisheries Research Board of Canada, Bulletin 167, 49–56.Standard Methods for the Examination of Water and Wastewater, 18th edition, AWWA, APHA, Water pollution control federation, Washington, DC, 1992.Methods for Chemical Analysis of Water and Wastes, U.S. EPA - 600/4-79-020, March 1979.
